name: Idard Fattæ - Ældartæ

abilities.name: Precision Shot
abilities.text: Improved missile weapon damage for an extended period. These values are further modified by the unit itself.

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

abilities.name: Barrage
abilities.text: Loose projectiles more frequently for an extended period of time.

abilities.name: Cantabrian Circle
abilities.text: The unit fires whilst riding in a circle.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Fire Whilst Moving
attributes.text: This unit can fire when mounted and moving.

attributes.name: Parthian Shot
attributes.text: This unit can fire all around and not just in-front of itself.

short: Long Arrows — Arcaragantes, these are archers - armed with the most advanced and long-range bow, later called the "Hun bow". Idard (long\distant). Fat (arrow/bullet), fattæ (arrow/bullet) - goes back to the ancient Iranian pat - "to fly".
history: Born from a tradition of raiding nomadic tribesmen, mounted archery became firmly established in the ancient world, leading to some highly effective battlefield units. While foot archers could be equipped with longer, more powerful bows, the mounted archer was still a formidable opponent thanks to the design of the composite bow. Constructed from a combination of wood, sinew and animal horn, the composite bow was far more effective than the traditional wooden variety. As its core offered greater flexibility, allowing the archer to draw its string back further and achieve a great range and power, the composite bow could find a target up to 35 metres away and pierce chainmail armour. Requiring great strength and stamina to use well, the composite bow demanded respect, care and attention. As military campaigns were often fought during the summer and autumn months, archers could rest their weapons during the winter - reconditioning the bodies before restringing and tensioning for future use.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
